item.title: Qatar Rewrites Its Gas Playbook With Old Tankers and New Tactics
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: Six months into a war that sowed upheaval in the Persian Gulf, Qatar found itself stuck. By late August, even limited shipments from the gas heavyweight had all but stopped following a projectile attack on one of its tankers outside the Strait of Hormuz. Pressure was growing, not only from energy-starved clients but also from inside an economy built on regular deliveries.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Yemen's Houthis vowed on Wednesday to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia, a day after a strike that sources said caused extensive damage to the headquarters of oil giant Saudi Aramco2223.SE.

item.title: Royal Navy’s Only Ice Patrol Ship Faces Uncertain Future After Defect
item.dc:creator: Malte Humpert
item.description: The Royal Navy’s only dedicated ice patrol ship has been towed from Teesside to Devonport following a reported defect, raising questions about Britain’s ability to maintain its maritime presence in the polar regions as the government works toward a replacement.

item.title: Trump Touts Taiwan-Alaska LNG Deal Taipei Hasn’t Finalized
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: President Donald Trump said Taiwan had agreed to buy 30% of the liquefied natural gas from a planned project in Alaska for 20 years, even as Taipei indicated that no binding commitments have been finalized.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Strikes Houthi Targets as Red Sea War Escalates
item.dc:creator: Mike Schuler
item.description: Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis said Saudi Arabia was attacking the Yemeni capital Sanaa on Tuesday after a Saudi-led coalition warned civilians to stay away from an oil depot on the city's outskirts, part of a rapidly escalating war between the sides.
